tag: an unexplained commitment is stored instead of refused
why: A number on a governance record with no basis is read by a later round as a measurement, which is the defect this whole method removes. `if False and ...` leaves the message intact, so the leg asserts the BEHAVIOUR — a 422 — rather than the presence of the sentence.

tag: a submitter's confidence stops being labelled DECLARED
why: THE ONE THING A LATER READER MUST NOT GET WRONG. CAPACITY_FACULTY_MODEL §2 admits a probability about SELF as a measurement and refuses one about another's choice; a figure a SUBMITTER hands over is neither measured nor about self-performance, so an unlabelled 0.7 on a governance record becomes a measurement this platform never made.

tag: the commitment stops travelling with the submission
why: A promise stored on a record and absent from the response is a fact rendered nowhere — the shape the method_check in this same file already had to be fixed for. The caller that MADE the promise is exactly who needs to see what was kept of it.

tag: the variance stops saying its rounds figure is derived
old: derived = (f"DERIVED, not counted: {elapsed_h} elapsed hours divided by the {median_h} h median "
new: derived = (f"{elapsed_h} elapsed hours over the {median_h} h median "
why: A ROUND IS NOT A CLOCK UNIT. Without the word and the divisor named, `rounds_equivalent` reads as a COUNT of rounds nobody counted — a figure carrying the name of something it did not measure, which is this repository's oldest rule about numbers.

tag: one of the two outcome sites stops recording the variance
old: _record_variance(c, now, "implemented")                   # W581 (FU-313) — the SECOND of two sites
new: pass  # W581 (FU-313) — the SECOND of two sites
why: THE SECOND-WRITER CLASS, which has cost this repository more rounds than any other: `status = "implemented"` is set in two places and a fix applied to one of them leaves the other silent. The leg asserts it over the AST of every function that marks a change implemented, so a third site added later is caught too.

tag: a variance is invented for a change nothing was promised about
new: if False and not isinstance(commitment, dict):
why: Then a change with no commitment gets a variance against `committed_rounds: None` — a measured outcome compared with a promise that was never made. 'No promise' and 'a promise of nothing' are different records and only one of them has a variance.

tag: the queue drops the promise, so it is invisible in flight
why: The queue is the list the growing tip reads. A commitment held only on the individual record is a promise nobody sees WHILE THE WORK IS IN FLIGHT, which is the whole reason for recording one rather than reporting it afterwards.

tag: the page stops rendering the promise
why: Clause (1) of this item's ACCEPT: the property is driven on the surface a person actually reads, never only on the API beneath it, because a writer fixed without its reader moves the untruth down a layer. W503's class, so the leg asserts the gate WITH its opening brace.

tag: the page renders a confidence without saying whether it was declared
why: §2's line then holds in the record and is LOST ON THE SURFACE. A reviewer looking at 70% on a card has no other way to know whether this platform measured it or a submitter asserted it, and that is the only distinction that makes the number admissible at all.

tag: orchestrate goes back to silently dropping what a caller promised
old:
committed_rounds: int | None = None
    confidence: float | None = None
    commitment_basis: str = ""
new: pass  # undeclared, so Pydantic discards whatever the caller sent
why: THE ROW'S ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT: an undeclared field is discarded and the caller still gets a 200, so a transformation could be promised in a number of rounds at a stated confidence and nothing anywhere held the promise. The platform-wide half — 206 models, none forbidding extras — is registered separately.
